intro_html: Brown sugar and sesame give this pork a sweet, nutty glaze that tastes like you fussed over it, when really the slow cooker did all the work. Each bowl carries 55 grams of protein over rice and broccoli for just $3.85 (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings at that price keeps the whole week easy on your budget.
cost_closing_html: About $3.85 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each serving runs about 607 calories with 55 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Sweet, nutty, and cheap enough that you can make it every week without a second thought. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Brown sugar and soy sauce make a glaze for almost nothing. A bag of brown sugar lasts for months and you use just a little each time.
Toasted sesame seeds are a small touch that makes the bowl look finished. One jar goes a long way, so buy it once.
Lean on pork loin at around $2 a pound to keep this bowl easy on the grocery budget.
make_it: Rub the pork loin with a little olive oil and set it in the slow cooker with the sliced onion.
Stir together the brown sugar and soy sauce, then pour it over the pork.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until fork-tender.
Shred the pork and stir it back through the glaze.
Steam the broccoli florets until just tender.
Serve over cooked white rice, sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds, and pack it up.
